query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attitude_complaint
per_column.rationale: A cabin-service complaint subtype directly implied by 'the most common cabin-service complaints'. Eliminating it (via improved crew behaviour) is the interventional lever the query is asking about.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness_complaint
per_column.rationale: Another decomposition of the cabin-service complaint treatment named in the query; responsiveness of service is a settable/improvable property, so it is an intervenable part of the treatment.

per_column.name: food_quality_complaint
per_column.rationale: Food/beverage service is part of cabin service; the complaint indicator is a treatment sub-component the airline can act on (mirrors existing 'Food & Beverages' rating).

per_column.name: seat_comfort_complaint
per_column.rationale: Seat comfort is a configurable cabin property and a plausible member of 'cabin-service complaints'; it is part of the treatment being eliminated, not a common cause of it.

per_column.name: service_recovery_attempted
per_column.rationale: Service recovery is undertaken in RESPONSE to a complaint, so it lies on the path complaint -> recovery -> rating. It is intervenable but is a mediator/downstream action, not a common cause of the complaint; per instructions it is not counted as a confounder.

per_column.name: traveller_type
per_column.rationale: Traveller segment (business vs leisure) plausibly drives both the propensity to file cabin-service complaints (differing expectations) and the Overall Rating independently, so it is a common cause. Not named in the query text, though it merely duplicates the pre-existing 'Type of Traveller' column, so it adds little new information.

per_column.name: flight_disruption_complaint
per_column.rationale: Flight disruption is NOT cabin service, so it is outside the treatment. A disrupted flight can both raise the rate of cabin-service complaints (frustrated passengers) and depress the Overall Rating, making it a plausible (if weak, since it is a self-reported complaint proxy) common cause to adjust for. Could instead be read as a competing cause rather than a strict confounder.

per_column.name: inflight_entertainment_complaint
per_column.rationale: Inflight entertainment is an in-cabin amenity the airline configures; it is best read as another sub-component of the cabin-service complaints being eliminated rather than a confounder.

judge.rationale: The treatment side of the interventional claim is satisfied: the added complaint indicators decompose the query's 'cabin-service complaints' into intervenable levers (crew attitude, responsiveness, food, seat comfort, entertainment) that an airline could actually set/change, so treatment_intervenable holds. However, the confounding side is thin. The bulk of the added columns are treatment decomposition, not common causes. Only traveller_type is a clean confounder not named in the query text, and it merely re-derives the pre-existing 'Type of Traveller' field, so it demonstrates little new capability. flight_disruption_complaint is at best a weak/ambiguous confounder (arguably just a competing cause), and service_recovery_attempted is a mediator (downstream of complaints) that must not be adjusted for. Because the capability under test is surfacing genuine, previously-unnamed confounders, the set only weakly realises it: confounder_quality is low.
